## Prerequisites

K3Desktop only requires **Docker** to be installed and running. There is no k3d CLI, Helm CLI,
or kubectl dependency — all cluster operations run via embedded Go packages.

- **Docker Desktop** (macOS/Windows) or **Docker Engine** (Linux) — [docker.com](https://www.docker.com/get-started)

Make sure the Docker daemon is running before launching K3Desktop.

## Download

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="macOS">

Download the latest `.zip` from the [Releases page](https://github.com/k3desktop/k3desktop/releases).

1. Unzip the archive
2. Drag **K3Desktop.app** to `/Applications`
3. On first launch, right-click → **Open** to bypass Gatekeeper (unsigned app)

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="Linux">

Download the binary for your architecture from the [Releases page](https://github.com/k3desktop/k3desktop/releases).

```bash
chmod +x k3desktop-linux-amd64
./k3desktop-linux-amd64
```

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="Windows">

<Aside type="caution">Windows support is planned for a future release.</Aside>

  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

## First Launch

1. Open K3Desktop
2. The **Clusters** page opens — empty on first run
3. Click **New Cluster** to create your first cluster
4. Once ready, click **Export Kubeconfig** to add it to `~/.kube/config`

Your cluster is ready. Use `kubectl`, `k9s`, or any Kubernetes tool as normal.
Define and deploy reusable Helm application stacks with K3Desktop Blueprints.

import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

## Overview

**Blueprints** are reusable Helm deployment templates stored locally at
`~/.config/k3desktop/blueprints/`. A blueprint defines one or more Helm charts
to install together, forming a complete application stack.

## Creating a Blueprint

Click **New Blueprint** and fill in:

- **Name** — blueprint identifier (becomes the filename `<name>.yaml`)
- **Charts** — one or more Helm charts with their configuration

Each chart entry includes:
- **Chart** — Helm chart reference (e.g. `stable/nginx-ingress`, OCI ref, or local path)
- **Release name** — Helm release name in the target cluster
- **Namespace** — Kubernetes namespace (created if it doesn't exist)
- **Values** — inline YAML values (equivalent to `-f values.yaml`)

Example blueprint YAML:

```yaml
name: monitoring-stack
charts:
  - chart: prometheus-community/kube-prometheus-stack
    release: prometheus
    namespace: monitoring
    values: |
      grafana:
        enabled: true
        adminPassword: admin
  - chart: prometheus-community/prometheus-adapter
    release: prometheus-adapter
    namespace: monitoring
```

## Deploying a Blueprint

1. Open the blueprint
2. Click **Deploy**
3. Select the target cluster
4. K3Desktop runs Helm upgrade-or-install for each chart in order

Deployment runs asynchronously. Progress and errors appear in the log panel.

<Aside type="tip">
Blueprints use upgrade-or-install logic: if the release already exists it is upgraded,
otherwise it is freshly installed with namespace creation enabled.
</Aside>

## Managing Blueprints

| Action | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| **Save** | Persist changes to `~/.config/k3desktop/blueprints/<name>.yaml` |
| **Delete** | Remove the blueprint file (does not uninstall deployed releases) |
| **Deploy** | Run Helm install/upgrade for all charts in the blueprint |

<Aside type="caution">
Deleting a blueprint does not remove the Helm releases already deployed to your clusters.
Use `helm uninstall` or kubectl to clean those up.
</Aside>
Create, start, stop, and delete k3d clusters with K3Desktop.

import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

## Overview

The **Clusters** page is the home screen of K3Desktop. It lists all k3d clusters on your machine
and lets you create new ones or manage existing ones.

## Creating a Cluster

Click **New Cluster** to open the creation dialog. Two modes are available:

### Simple Mode

Fill in:
- **Name** — unique cluster identifier (lowercase, no spaces)
- **Servers** — number of control-plane nodes (default: 1)
- **Agents** — number of worker nodes (default: 0)
- **k3s Image** — Kubernetes version (leave blank for latest)
- **API Port** — host port mapped to the k3s API server (leave blank for auto-assign)

### Advanced Mode

Full YAML configuration editor with syntax highlighting, linting, and auto-indent.
Uses the [k3d config file format](https://k3d.io/stable/usage/configfile/).

<Aside type="tip">
Advanced mode is useful for reproducible cluster setups — save your YAML config to version control.
</Aside>

## Cluster Creation Progress

Cluster creation runs asynchronously. A progress indicator appears while k3d provisions
the cluster. If creation fails, K3Desktop automatically rolls back any partially created resources.

## Cluster Actions

| Action | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| **Start** | Start a stopped cluster |
| **Stop** | Stop a running cluster (preserves data) |
| **Delete** | Permanently delete the cluster and all its nodes |
| **Export Kubeconfig** | Merge cluster credentials into `~/.kube/config` |

<Aside type="caution">
Deleting a cluster removes all workloads and persistent data inside it. This cannot be undone.
</Aside>
Export kubeconfigs and manage Kubernetes contexts in K3Desktop.

## Overview

The **Kubeconfig** page lets you manage the `~/.kube/config` file — the standard Kubernetes
credential file used by `kubectl`, `helm`, `k9s`, and other tools.

## Exporting a Cluster's Kubeconfig

From the Clusters page, click **Export Kubeconfig** on any running cluster.
K3Desktop merges the cluster's credentials into `~/.kube/config`, creating or updating
the relevant context, cluster, and user entries.

## Viewing the Raw Kubeconfig

The **Kubeconfig** page shows the full `~/.kube/config` as YAML.
This is read-only — edit the file directly if you need to make manual changes.

## Context Management

| Action | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| **Set Active** | Switch `current-context` to the selected context |
| **Delete** | Remove the context (and its associated cluster/user entries if orphaned) |

<Aside type="tip">
After creating a cluster, export its kubeconfig and set it as the active context.
Then `kubectl get nodes` will target that cluster.
</Aside>

## Multiple Clusters

K3Desktop supports multiple clusters simultaneously. Each export merges cleanly — contexts
are namespaced by cluster name so they don't overwrite each other.

```bash
# List all contexts after exporting multiple clusters
kubectl config get-contexts
```

The **Nodes** page shows all nodes in the selected cluster, including their role (server/agent)
and current status (running/stopped).

Click **Add Node** to attach a new agent (worker) node to the selected cluster.

Save and reuse cluster configuration profiles in K3Desktop.

import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

## Overview

**Profiles** are saved k3d cluster configurations stored as YAML files at
`~/.config/k3desktop/profiles/`. A profile captures a full cluster spec — node counts,
port mappings, volumes, environment variables, k3s args, registry setup, and more —
so you can recreate identical clusters with one click.

## Creating a Profile

Open **New Cluster → Advanced** mode. Configure your cluster, then click **Save as Profile**
and give it a name. The current editor YAML is saved to `~/.config/k3desktop/profiles/<name>.yaml`.

You can also create or edit profiles directly from the **Profiles** page.

## Loading a Profile

From **New Cluster → Advanced** mode, click **Load Profile** and select a saved profile.
The editor populates with the profile's YAML, which you can further edit before creating.

## Importing a Profile

Click **Import** on the Profiles page. A file picker opens — select any valid k3d v1alpha5
YAML file from your filesystem. K3Desktop validates the YAML and copies it into the profiles
directory. If a profile with the same name already exists, the imported file is saved with a
`-imported` suffix.

<Aside type="tip">
Profiles are plain YAML files. You can version-control them, share them with teammates,
or write them by hand using the [k3d config file reference](https://k3d.io/stable/usage/configfile/).
</Aside>

## Profile YAML Format

Profiles use the [k3d `Simple` config format](https://k3d.io/stable/usage/configfile/) (v1alpha5):

```yaml
apiVersion: k3d.io/v1alpha5
kind: Simple
metadata:
  name: my-cluster
servers: 1
agents: 2
image: rancher/k3s:v1.29.0-k3s1
ports:
  - port: 8080:80
    nodeFilters:
      - loadbalancer
volumes:
  - volume: /tmp/data:/data
    nodeFilters:
      - all
options:
  k3d:
    wait: true
  kubeconfig:
    updateDefaultKubeconfig: true
    switchCurrentContext: true
```

## Managing Profiles

| Action | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| **Save** | Persist edits to `~/.config/k3desktop/profiles/<name>.yaml` |
| **Delete** | Remove the profile file |
| **Import** | Copy an external YAML file into the profiles directory |
| **Load** | Populate the cluster creation editor with the profile's config |
Create and manage local k3d container registries.

import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

## Overview

K3Desktop lets you create local k3d container registries — private Docker-compatible registries
that run entirely on your machine. No Docker Hub rate limits, no credentials needed.

## Creating a Registry

Click **New Registry** and fill in:

- **Name** — registry identifier (becomes the hostname `k3d-<name>`)
- **Port** — host port for the registry (leave blank to auto-assign a random port)

After creation the registry is accessible at `localhost:<port>` from your host machine.

## Using a Registry with a Cluster

To let a cluster pull images from your local registry, the registry must be on the same
k3d network as the cluster. Wire this up by referencing the registry in your cluster config:

```yaml
# k3d cluster config
apiVersion: k3d.io/v1alpha5
kind: Simple
registries:
  use:
    - k3d-myregistry:5000
```

## Pushing Images

```bash
# Tag and push to local registry
docker tag myapp:latest k3d-myregistry:5000/myapp:latest
docker push k3d-myregistry:5000/myapp:latest
```

Your cluster can now pull `k3d-myregistry:5000/myapp:latest` directly.

## Deleting a Registry

Click **Delete** on the registry row. K3Desktop disconnects the registry from all cluster
networks before deletion to avoid dangling endpoint errors.

<Aside type="tip">
Registries are persistent — they survive cluster restarts and can be shared across multiple clusters.
</Aside>

## Vue d'ensemble

La page **Nodes** affiche tous les nœuds du cluster sélectionné, y compris leur rôle (serveur/agent) et leur état actuel (en cours d'exécution/arrêté).

## Ajouter un Nœud Agent

Cliquez sur **Ajouter un Nœud** pour rattacher un nouveau nœud agent (worker) au cluster sélectionné.
Le nouveau nœud rejoint immédiatement le cluster et est visible via `kubectl get nodes`.

## Actions sur les Nœuds

| Action | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| **Démarrer** | Démarrer un nœud arrêté |
| **Arrêter** | Arrêter un nœud en cours d'exécution |
| **Supprimer** | Supprimer un nœud agent du cluster |

</Aside>

## Rôles des Nœuds

- **server** — nœud control-plane k3s. Exécute l'API server, le scheduler et le controller manager.

## Vue d'ensemble

K3Desktop vous permet de créer des registres de conteneurs k3d locaux — des registres compatibles Docker privés qui fonctionnent entièrement sur votre machine. Pas de limites Docker Hub, pas de credentials nécessaires.

## Création d'un Registre

Cliquez sur **Nouveau Registre** et remplissez :

- **Nom** — identifiant du registre (devient le nom d'hôte `k3d-<nom>`)
- **Port** — port hôte pour le registre (laisser vide pour attribution aléatoire)

Après création, le registre est accessible sur `localhost:<port>` depuis votre machine.

## Utiliser un Registre avec un Cluster

Pour permettre à un cluster de tirer des images depuis le registre local, le registre doit être sur le même réseau k3d que le cluster. Reliez-les en référencant le registre dans la config du cluster :

```yaml
# config cluster k3d
apiVersion: k3d.io/v1alpha5
kind: Simple
registries:
	use:
		- k3d-monRegistre:5000
```

## Pousser des Images

```bash
# Taguer et pousser vers le registre local
docker tag myapp:latest k3d-monRegistre:5000/myapp:latest
docker push k3d-monRegistre:5000/myapp:latest
```

Votre cluster peut maintenant tirer directement `k3d-monRegistre:5000/myapp:latest`.

## Suppression d'un Registre

Cliquez sur **Supprimer** sur la ligne du registre. K3Desktop déconnecte le registre de tous les réseaux de cluster avant suppression pour éviter les erreurs d'endpoint en suspens.

<Aside type="tip">
Les registres sont persistants — ils survivent aux redémarrages de cluster et peuvent être partagés entre plusieurs clusters.
</Aside>

## Panoramica

I **Blueprint** sono template Helm riutilizzabili per il deploy, salvati localmente in
`~/.config/k3desktop/blueprints/`. Un blueprint definisce uno o più chart Helm da installare insieme, formando uno stack applicativo completo.

## Creazione di un Blueprint

Clicca su **Nuovo Blueprint** e compila:

- **Nome** — identificativo del blueprint (diventa il file `<nome>.yaml`)
- **Chart** — uno o più chart Helm con la loro configurazione

Ogni chart include:
- **Chart** — riferimento al chart Helm (es. `stable/nginx-ingress`, riferimento OCI o percorso locale)
- **Nome release** — nome della release Helm nel cluster di destinazione
- **Namespace** — namespace Kubernetes (creato se non esiste)
- **Valori** — valori YAML inline (equivalente a `-f values.yaml`)

Esempio di blueprint YAML:

```yaml
name: monitoring-stack
charts:
	- chart: prometheus-community/kube-prometheus-stack
		release: prometheus
		namespace: monitoring
		values: |
			grafana:
				enabled: true
				adminPassword: admin
	- chart: prometheus-community/prometheus-adapter
		release: prometheus-adapter
		namespace: monitoring
```

## Distribuzione di un Blueprint

1. Apri il blueprint
2. Clicca **Distribuisci**
3. Seleziona il cluster di destinazione
4. K3Desktop esegue Helm upgrade-or-install per ogni chart in ordine

La distribuzione è asincrona. Avanzamento ed errori appaiono nel pannello log.

<Aside type="tip">
I blueprint usano la logica upgrade-or-install: se la release esiste già viene aggiornata,
altrimenti viene installata da zero con creazione del namespace abilitata.
</Aside>

## Panoramica

La pagina **Clusters** è la schermata principale di K3Desktop. Elenca tutti i cluster k3d sulla tua macchina e permette di crearne di nuovi o gestire quelli esistenti.

## Creazione di un Cluster

Clicca su **Nuovo Cluster** per aprire la finestra di creazione. Sono disponibili due modalità:

### Modalità Semplice

Compila:
- **Nome** — identificativo univoco del cluster (minuscolo, senza spazi)
- **Server** — numero di nodi control-plane (default: 1)
- **Agent** — numero di nodi worker (default: 0)
- **Immagine k3s** — versione Kubernetes (lascia vuoto per l'ultima)
- **Porta API** — porta host mappata sull'API server k3s (lascia vuoto per assegnazione automatica)

### Modalità Avanzata

Editor YAML completo con evidenziazione sintassi, linting e auto-indentazione.
Usa il [formato file di configurazione k3d](https://k3d.io/stable/usage/configfile/).

<Aside type="tip">
La modalità avanzata è utile per setup cluster riproducibili — salva il tuo YAML sotto version control.
</Aside>

## Avanzamento Creazione Cluster

La creazione del cluster è asincrona. Un indicatore di avanzamento appare mentre k3d provvede al provisioning. Se la creazione fallisce, K3Desktop effettua automaticamente il rollback delle risorse parzialmente create.

## Azioni Cluster

| Azione | Descrizione |
|--------|-------------|
| **Avvia** | Avvia un cluster fermo |
| **Ferma** | Ferma un cluster attivo (i dati vengono preservati) |
| **Elimina** | Elimina definitivamente il cluster e tutti i suoi nodi |
| **Esporta Kubeconfig** | Unisce le credenziali del cluster in `~/.kube/config` |

<Aside type="caution">
Eliminare un cluster rimuove tutti i workload e i dati persistenti al suo interno. Questa operazione è irreversibile.
</Aside>

K3Desktop ti permette di creare registry container k3d locali — registry Docker-compatibili privati che girano interamente sulla tua macchina. Nessun limite Docker Hub, nessuna credenziale necessaria.

## Creazione di un Registry

Clicca su **Nuovo Registry** e compila:

- **Nome** — identificativo del registry (diventa l'hostname `k3d-<nome>`)
- **Porta** — porta host per il registry (lascia vuoto per assegnazione casuale)

## Usare un Registry con un Cluster

Per permettere a un cluster di scaricare immagini dal registry locale, il registry deve essere sulla stessa rete k3d del cluster. Collega tutto referenziando il registry nella config del cluster:

```yaml
# config cluster k3d
apiVersion: k3d.io/v1alpha5
kind: Simple
registries:
	use:
		- k3d-mioRegistry:5000
```

```bash
# Tagga e push su registry locale

docker push k3d-mioRegistry:5000/myapp:latest
```

Ora il cluster può scaricare direttamente `k3d-mioRegistry:5000/myapp:latest`.

## Eliminazione di un Registry
